PMID:41158719.topic: ENT casualty management of common acute presentations
PMID:41158719.setting: ENT casualty service of a tertiary referral hospital (Mater Dei Hospital, Msida)
PMID:41158719.standard: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries (otitis externa), ENT UK nasal trauma guidance, ENT UK position statement and AAO-HNS guideline (SSNHL), British Rhinological Society epistaxis guideline; e.g. audiogram within 24 hours for SSNHL, nasal fracture review within 7 days

cycle1.dates: 5 weeks (10 consecutive weeks over both cycles)
cycle1.result: Tympanic membrane integrity documented in otitis externa 34.3%; nasal fracture reviewed within 7 days 58.3%, MUA within 14 days 92.9%; SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 33.3%; epistaxis cautery for visible vessel 87.2%, documentation of counselling 28.0%.

PMID:41158719.intervention: Web-based ENT toolkit with QR-code access in casualty, condition-specific pathways, structured documentation templates, procedure checklists and diagrams, introduced to FY doctors at induction with a short training session.

cycle2.result: Tympanic membrane documentation 67.7% (p = 0.002); nasal fracture review within 7 days 94.7% (p = 0.006), MUA within 14 days 100% (p = 0.31); SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 80.0% (p = 0.09); epistaxis cautery 98.1% (p = 0.03), counselling documented 46.0%.

PMID:41158719.other_findings: Unnecessary imaging and swabbing fell (e.g. avoidance of unnecessary nasal imaging 41.7% to 84.2%); counselling documentation in epistaxis stayed low at 46.0%. Staff confidence rose from 2.4/5 to 4.1/5; cycles involved different FY cohorts.

PMID:16737522.setting: National postal survey of UK spinal surgeons (members of BASS or Society for Back Pain Research)

cycle1.result: Survey of practice: 79% had a routine post-operative regime, 35% gave written instructions, 55% did not refer for physiotherapy after discharge; restrictions on lifting, sitting and driving varied widely.

PMID:16737522.other_findings: 89 surgeons surveyed, 57% usable response; weak correlation between individual surgeons' activity restriction recommendations.

PMID:40276417.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure in falls assessment
PMID:40276417.setting: Orthopaedic rehabilitation ward, district general hospital in North East England
PMID:40276417.standard: NICE falls guidance: completion of falls assessment and lying and standing blood pressure measurement; target 100%

cycle1.result: Falls assessment completed 38/41 (93%); lying and standing BP recorded 14/41 (34%).

PMID:40276417.intervention: Cycle 1 results presented at departmental teaching, daily reminders at the morning huddle, educational flyers and targeted education for doctors, nurses and healthcare staff.

cycle2.result: Falls assessment completed 40/41 (98%) (p = 0.61); lying and standing BP recorded 28/41 (68%) (p = 0.004).

PMID:40276417.other_findings: Systolic drop of 20 mmHg or more found in 5/14 (36%) then 13/28 (46.4%) of those measured. LSBP was sometimes marked as completed in the falls assessment when it was not done.

PMID:41473354.specialty: Orthopaedics – Oncology (giant cell tumour of bone)
PMID:41473354.topic: Neoadjuvant denosumab biosimilar in giant cell tumour of bone
PMID:41473354.setting: Tertiary cancer centre (Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya Cancer Centre and Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital, Varanasi)

cycle1.result: Retrospective case series: two doses of denosumab biosimilar gave a mean lesion size reduction of 17.75% ± 8.029%; sclerotic rim in all 17 cases; local recurrence 2/17 (11%) and distant recurrence 2/17 (11%).

PMID:41473354.other_findings: No hypocalcaemia or osteonecrosis; both recurrences were in previously recurrent cases treated by repeat extended curettage.

PMID:41458347.topic: Fluoroscopy radiation exposure in distal radius fracture fixation
PMID:41458347.setting: William Harvey Hospital, Ashford, Kent (East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Mean screening time 24 seconds (range 0.1-111), mean 43 exposures (range 5-209), mean DAP 4.75 µGy·m² (range 0.31-29.26), mean air kerma 0.26 (range 0.01-9).

PMID:41458347.other_findings: No significant differences by surgeon grade (registrar vs consultant) or fracture type; 39 of 145 cases excluded because no fluoroscopy data were saved. No standard or diagnostic reference level was available to audit against.

PMID:31817489.specialty: Oral and maxillofacial surgery / trauma epidemiology
PMID:31817489.topic: Head and neck trauma admissions epidemiology
PMID:31817489.setting: Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam (national referral hospital)

cycle1.result: Most common diagnoses: S02 fracture of skull and facial bones 277 (44.1%), S05 injury of eye and orbit 114 (18.2%), S09 other head injuries 77 (12.3%); 81.2% male.

PMID:31817489.other_findings: Head and neck trauma was 2.55% of all trauma admissions; no seasonal trend.

PMID:41487762.setting: Poole Hospital, district general hospital (University Hospitals Dorset)
PMID:41487762.standard: Clark's Positioning in Radiography criteria for lateral wrist radiographs (styloid superimposition, anatomical inclusion, piso-scapho-capitate relationship); target 80% for each

cycle1.result: Styloid superimposition 72% (36/50); anatomical inclusion 98% (49/50); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 50% (25/50).

PMID:41487762.intervention: Poster on positioning technique in the radiology department and trauma meeting rooms, and a formal teaching session by an associate specialist hand surgeon for radiographers and orthopaedic doctors.

cycle2.result: Styloid superimposition 92% (46/50) (p = 0.047); anatomical inclusion 100% (50/50) (p = 0.992); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 82% (41/50) (p = 0.014).

PMID:41487762.other_findings: All three standards met the 80% target at re-audit; the study did not assess whether any injuries were missed.

PMID:41250712.setting: Emergency department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham (tertiary centre)
PMID:41250712.standard: BESS guideline and local hospital policy: orthogonal post-reduction views (AP plus axillary or scapular Y view)

cycle1.result: Adequate orthogonal post-reduction radiographs in 5/22 (22.7%, 95% CI 10.1-43.4); 17/22 (77.3%) inadequate, with inadequacy recognised by resident doctors in 2/17 (11.8%).

PMID:41250712.other_findings: No imaging request explicitly specified two orthogonal views and no repeat imaging was obtained in the ED; education and re-audit are planned.

PMID:35175142.setting: Elective arthroplasty unit, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:35175142.standard: Hyponatraemia protocol based on NICE guidance (sodium cut-off 133 mmol/l per local guidance); no numeric target stated

cycle1.result: Hyponatraemia in 36 (12%); only 38% of hyponatraemic patients investigated, 33% had endocrine input; mean 3.6 days to endocrine referral; length of stay 7.7 vs 4.6 days; 4 of 11 profound cases admitted to critical care (8 days in total).

PMID:35175142.intervention: Direct endocrine pathway developed with endocrinology based on NICE guidance: protocol poster displayed in clinical areas and agreement for same-day endocrine review of arthroplasty patients referred via ICE.

cycle2.result: Hyponatraemia in 31 (11.7%); all 3 profound cases investigated and referred to endocrinology; mean 2.3 days to endocrine referral; length of stay reduced by 0.7 days (p = 0.008144); no critical care admissions (p = 0.031622).

PMID:35175142.other_findings: Hyponatraemia was more common after knee than hip replacement and in older patients in both cycles; symptoms and fluids were not assessed in cycle 2.

PMID:37731682.setting: Mansell Road Practice, primary care general practice, London
PMID:37731682.standard: NICE guidance on bone protection (bisphosphonates first line) after fragility fracture

cycle1.result: 33/47 on bone protection agents (26 bisphosphonate plus calcium/vitamin D, 7 bisphosphonate alone); 2 on calcium/vitamin D alone; 12/47 on neither therapy.

PMID:37731682.intervention: Educational poster on recognition and coding of fragility fractures; untreated patients reviewed individually and started on treatment, referred for DEXA or specialist advice.
PMID:37731682.other_findings: Of the 12 untreated, 2 were miscoded; of the remaining 10, 4 were referred for DEXA, 2 referred for zoledronic acid and 1 started alendronic acid. No re-audit reported.

PMID:39982631.setting: Consultant orthopaedic surgeons in training hospitals across the Republic of Ireland (online survey)

cycle1.result: Survey of practice (response 69/96, 72%): 72.5% aware of local VTE guidelines, 37.8% aware of national guidelines; 90% routinely used mechanical prophylaxis; 74% used LMWH for inpatients; 82.6% discharged patients on extended chemical prophylaxis.

PMID:39982631.other_findings: No national trauma VTE guideline existed in Ireland at the time; 67% agreed that defensive medicine drives VTE prophylaxis emphasis; agents and durations were highly heterogeneous.

PMID:36059306.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley
PMID:36059306.standard: BOA guidance on ward round documentation (patient ID and name, ward round clinician, documenting clinician, grade, date, time, whom to contact)

cycle1.result: Paper notes: patient ID and name 29 (65.91%); documenting clinician 17 (38.64%); time of ward round 26 (59.09%); grade of ward round clinician 18 (40.91%); whom to contact 0 (0%) (percentages as stated).

PMID:36059306.intervention: Introduction of electronic ward round record keeping.

cycle2.result: Electronic records: patient ID and name, ward round clinician, documenting clinician, date, time and grade all 34 (100%); whom to contact 5 (14.70%).

PMID:36059306.other_findings: Staff satisfaction and educational value scores (44 staff surveyed) were higher for electronic records; documentation of whom to contact stayed poor.

PMID:38313878.setting: Trauma theatre, Trauma and Orthopaedic Department of a district general hospital (Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley)
PMID:38313878.standard: BOAST guidance on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets (2021): document skin condition and isolation method, pressure SBP + 50-100 mmHg upper limb and + 70-130 mmHg lower limb in adults, ischaemic time under 120 minutes

cycle1.result: Skin status documented 37%; isolation method documented 43%; tourniquet pressure documented 71%; pressure within BOAST safe limit 25%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

PMID:38313878.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; tourniquet details made a mandatory part of the electronic operation note template; labels on tourniquet machines to calculate pressure; BOAST guidance posted in the theatre doctors' office.

cycle2.result: Skin status documented 69% (p = 0.004); isolation method 74% (p = 0.003); pressure documented 94% (p = 0.003); pressure within BOAST safe limit 75%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

PMID:38313878.other_findings: Mean pressure above SBP fell from 125.9 to 99.9 mmHg (upper limb) and 154.2 to 121.7 mmHg (lower limb); about 25% still used pressures above the recommended range and surgeons not using the template still omitted details.

PMID:34513388.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure in falls assessment
PMID:34513388.setting: Orthopaedics department (ethical approval from Salisbury District Hospital)
PMID:34513388.standard: NICE guidelines on falls in older people: lying and standing blood pressure measurement; RCP FFAP guidance on LSBP procedure

cycle1.result: LSBP measured in 16 (32%); correctly documented in 12/16 (75%).

PMID:34513388.intervention: Results presented at geriatric medicine mortality meeting with root cause analysis; flyers and posters on wards, teaching sessions for ward staff on LSBP measurement and recording on POET, and aide-memoires placed around wards.

cycle2.result: LSBP measured in 45 (83.3%) (p < 0.0001); correctly documented in 45 (100%) (p = 0.0035).

PMID:34513388.other_findings: Root cause analysis found insufficient staff training and need for assistance to stand patients post-operatively.

PMID:41195409.setting: Elective orthopaedic ward, University College London Hospitals
PMID:41195409.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidance and PRSB eDischarge Summary Standard: investigation (imaging) results included in discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Imaging results documented in 0/144 (0%) discharge summaries.

PMID:41195409.intervention: Audit feedback poster on national standards for resident doctors, and a mandatory 'diagnostic imaging' field added to the electronic discharge summary template.

cycle2.result: Imaging results documented in 118/127 (92.9%) discharge summaries.

PMID:41195409.other_findings: Accuracy and clinical usefulness of the documented imaging were not assessed; trauma admissions were excluded.

PMID:41492587.topic: Neurovascular assessment documentation in limb fractures
PMID:41492587.setting: Russell Hall Hospital (Trauma and Orthopaedic admissions)
PMID:41492587.standard: BOAST Peripheral Nerve Injury guideline (December 2021): documentation of specific nerve and arterial status; target 100%

cycle1.result: Any NV documentation 43/49 (87.8%); detailed neurological findings 19/49 (38.8%); detailed vascular findings 13/49 (26.5%).

PMID:41492587.intervention: Single educational awareness presentation on the consequences of poor NV assessment (May 2024).

cycle2.result: Any NV documentation 47/48 (97.9%) (p = 0.053); detailed neurological findings 26/48 (54.2%) (p = 0.129); detailed vascular findings 22/48 (45.8%) (p = 0.048).

PMID:41492587.other_findings: Many entries still used the nonspecific phrase 'NV intact' rather than nerve-specific and arterial details.

PMID:23725954.topic: Empiric antimicrobial prescribing in trauma ICU
PMID:23725954.setting: Level I Trauma Intensive Care Unit, Inkosi Albert Luthuli Central Hospital, Durban
PMID:23725954.standard: Local surveillance-based empiric antimicrobial policy with antimicrobial stewardship

cycle1.result: Of 101 empiric and 14 directed prescriptions, excluding multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter, 87 (93.5%) were appropriate and 6 (6.5%) incorrect; ultrabroad-spectrum combination therapy used in 11 patients but necessary in only 2.

PMID:23725954.other_findings: 106/227 (46.6%) patients had culture-positive isolates; ESBL in 19% of E. coli and 25% of Klebsiella; 18 MRSA isolates. Abstract only.

PMID:34417002.setting: Pinderfields General Hospital, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general hospital)
PMID:34417002.standard: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission (National Hip Fracture Database)

cycle1.result: Surgery within 36 hours 54%; mean time to surgery 43.68 hours; BPT achieved in 45.7%; trust ranked 152/160 for time to surgery.

PMID:34417002.intervention: Anaesthetic 'hot week' introduced in January 2018: the same anaesthetist covers hip fracture lists, attends trauma meeting, liaises with orthopaedic and orthogeriatric teams and advises on medical optimisation.

cycle2.result: Surgery within 36 hours 87.5%; mean time to surgery 25.11 hours; BPT achieved in 84%; ranking rose to 20th for time to surgery and 18th for BPT.

PMID:34417002.other_findings: Rescheduled operations fell from 126 to 31 and mean length of stay fell by 5.1 days; mortality unchanged. The unit sees on average 551 hip fractures a year. Abstract only.
